FLOODING RESCUES: Chattanooga Fire’s Swiftwater Rescue Team was deployed to flooding early Thursday morning (11/5/26) to help search for anyone in need of assistance. Battalion Chief Chris Warren captured this footage. Our firefighters are part of a large response by many agencies to flooding in TN and North GA.  At 1:30 AM, the CFD received a mutual aid request for swiftwater personnel to respond to the area of McCaysville, GA and Copperhill, TN. One six-man team answered the call. They’ve rescued 11 people and two dogs.  Rescues and evacuations are ongoing.

Meet Ciraea Nilsen and Nakisha Jones. They are two of the many participants who recently completed the Parent Academy program offered by the Office of Community Health. Parent Academy is a free 8-week program designed to empower parents and caregivers with the tools to support their children’s academic, social, and emotional development. Both women are returning participants who came back because of the resources and support. They valued learning about options they didn’t know existed and enjoyed meeting community partners who exposed them to resources to help support their family. Ciraea's main takeaway was the number of resources she hadn’t known about. She named two in particular: life insurance and further schooling. She wants to look into life insurance now, even though she’s young, so her daughter has nothing to worry about. She also plans to go back to school. Nakisha expressed that the information she's learned has helped her with everyday challenges and hopes to take this program again!  Key Program Highlights: 🌟Educational Growth: Practical tools and actionable strategies for home learning. 🌟Financial Literacy: Workshops on budgeting fundamentals and path to homeownership. 🌟Community Networking: Direct links to local support networks and resources. Congratulations to Battalion Chief Travis Williams as he starts the next exciting chapter of his illustrious career in the fire service! Everyone at the Chattanooga Fire Department wishes him all the best!Please join us in welcoming Travis Williams as the Town of Signal Mountain’s new Fire Chief!  Chief Williams joins us after a 25-year career with the Chattanooga Fire Department, where he worked his way up from firefighter to Safety Chief and, most recently, Battalion Chief overseeing six fire halls. He also served in the U.S. Navy as an Engineman. Along the way, he has led complex emergency responses, championed firefighter health, safety, and wellness programs, and earned the respect of the crews he has led. The Signal Mountain Fire Fighters Association, IAFF Local 3759, and leaders from the Chattanooga Fire Department and the Hamilton County Sheriff’s Office all speak highly of his integrity and character. In Chief Williams’ words: “I am looking forward to working with the firefighters to make an already outstanding department even better. I appreciate the opportunity to serve the citizens of Signal Mountain. I am excited to get started.” Welcome to the Mountain, Chief! If you see him around town, say hello. 👋 #SignalMountain #SignalMountainTN #SMFD #WelcomeChiefWilliams

Shooting - 1600 block Rossville Avenue CHATTANOOGA, Tenn.  –  The Chattanooga Police Department (CPD) is investigating a shooting that occurred on November 1, 2026, at approximately 2:30 a.m. on the 1600 block of Rossville Avenue. Officers responded to the scene and located a 17-year-old male suffering from a gunshot wound. Shortly after, investigators learned a second victim, a 19-year-old male, had arrived at a nearby hospital by private vehicle. Both victims sustained non-life-threatening injuries.   This remains an active and ongoing investigation.  CPD’s Homicide Unit responded to lead the investigation and the Crime Scene Unit processed the scene for evidence. All active leads are being followed up on.  Anyone with information is asked to contact the Chattanooga Police Department at 423-698-2525. #CPDnews

Big Soddy Creek Gulf Nature Walk Take a refreshing stroll along Big Soddy Creek on a flat, wide gravel trail suitable for all skill levels. We will be exploring Big Soddy Creek Gulf. While the main route is level and even, side areas can feature uneven ground or wet spots.

National crash records show that children ages 4-8 are at 10 times higher risk of being hit by a driver on Halloween night compared to other evenings. 🎃 Adult supervision for children at  all times. 🎃Always walk on sidewalks. Check out this spooky, foggy morning at Heritage Park! Heritage Park is home to a special grassland ecosystem—a limestone fen. In partnership with the Southeastern Grassland Institute (SGI), the City of Chattanooga Natural Resources team works to manage this pocket-sized grassland to support biodiversity and help manage natural flooding. Grasslands, prairies, and savannahs used to dominate the southeastern United States, but over the last 300 years, they have rapidly disappeared. These ecosystems contain incredible plant diversity and support a wide array of animal and insect species. By incorporating this pocket grassland, we are providing habitat for wildlife, adding beauty and interest to the park, and helping filter stormwater runoff. So much history!BROWN’S FERRY (Tenn.) THEN & NOW — In this illustration from Harper’s Weekly via a British sketch artist, U.S. Army soldiers cross a pontoon bridge over the Tennessee River on Oct. 26, 1863. (Lookout Mountain looms in the background.) They have opened “The Cracker Line” into Chattanooga, thus ending the Confederates’ siege. Said POW Val Giles of the 4th Texas about this crossing: “That evening we started to Chattanooga under heavy guard. We crossed the Tennessee River about four miles below Lookout Mountain. Near the middle of the bridge we were halted and formed in one rank on each side to let some General Officers and their escorts pass. General Grant and General Thomas rode in front followed by a long train of staff officers and couriers. “When General Grant reached the line of ragged, bloody, filthy, starving, despairing prisoners strung out on each side of the bridge, he lifted his hat over his head until he passed the last man of that living funeral cortège.” @topfans

Autumn wildflowers are in full bloom at East Lake Park! This hillside was previously turf grass lawn, which was costly to maintain and offered little erosion control or stormwater absorption above the park’s historic 90-year-old WPA drainage ditch. Inspired by the discovery of a rare Lady’s Tresses orchid on-site, the Natural Resources Team partnered with the Southeastern Grasslands Institute (SGI) to research historical flora and restore the slope with native meadow species. Right now, the hillside is blanketed with blooming Monarda punctata (spotted horsemint). Research from the Mt. Cuba Center shows that horsemint is an ecological powerhouse—not only supporting native pollinators, but also attracting beneficial predatory wasps that naturally control pest caterpillars and grubs. Take a walk to the top of East Lake Park to see the meadow in action before the seasonal blooms wrap up and let us know what pollinators you spot at the top of the hill! 🐝🌸 #chattanooga #cityinapark #nativeplants #spottedhorsemint #urbanecology

Chattanooga Police Officers Involved in Shooting, TBI Investigating CHATTANOOGA, Tenn. -- The Chattanooga Police Department (CPD) responded to a 9-1-1 call Friday that resulted in a man being shot. Shortly after 10:00 a.m., officers were dispatched to the 2900 block of Kings Point Road. Upon arrival, officers located a 31-year-old man with a firearm. Officers gave him verbal commands to drop the gun, but he refused. The man then fired a shot, resulting in a self-inflicted injury, and a CPD officer fired one shot. Hamilton County EMS transported the man to the hospital where he was listed in critical condition.  At the request of the Hamilton County District Attorney, the Tennessee Bureau of Investigation (TBI) is investigating the incident. The involved officers were placed on paid administrative leave per standard policy requirements. This information is preliminary and subject to change as the investigation continues. #CPDnews

In order to identify and keep track of individual birds, scientists put aluminum or colored bands on birds’ legs. Similar to the license plate on a car, each aluminum band is engraved with a unique set of numbers. This helps us track important data such as migratory paths, general health, and lifespan. CPD Seeks Community's Assistance in Lookout Valley Shooting Investigation CHATTANOOGA, Tenn. -- The Chattanooga Police Department (CPD) is seeking the community's assistance in a Lookout Valley shooting investigation. At approximately 8:44 p.m. Thursday, CPD responded to reports of a shooting in the 300 block of Browns Ferry Road. CPD's Homicide and Crime Scene Units responded to investigate and process the scene. The preliminary investigation indicates the teenager first encountered the suspect while entering I-24 WB from Highway 27. The victim exited the interstate onto Browns Ferry Road, and the suspect began shooting at her from I-24. The suspect vehicle is described as a mid-size white SUV with a Georgia license plate. CPD asks anyone traveling on I-24 between Rossville Boulevard and Browns Ferry Road between 8:20 p.m. and 8:45 p.m. and may have witnessed this to contact the Chattanooga Police Department at (423) 698-2525. Specifically, if you saw a white SUV interacting with a black Silverado truck. Join us this Saturday morning at Greenway Farm from 7 - 11 am for an educational workshop all about bird banding!  What is bird banding, you ask? In order to identify and keep track of individual birds, scientists put aluminum or colored bands on birds' legs. Similar to the license plate on a car, each aluminum band is engraved with a unique set of numbers. This helps us track important data such as migratory paths, general health, and lifespan. This is a FREE all-ages workshop. Please share with your bird-loving friends and family. We would love an incredible turn out for this fun event.

CPD Investigating Deadly Crash Involving Pedestrians on E Main St. CHATTANOOGA, Tenn. -- The Chattanooga Police Department (CPD) is investigating a deadly crash involving pedestrians that resulted in one woman's death. At approximately 9:20 p.m. Saturday, CPD's Traffic Unit responded to reports of a crash involving pedestrians in the 300 block of E Main Street. The preliminary investigation indicates a group of people were using a crosswalk when a pickup truck hit two individuals.  Hamilton County EMS transported both patients to the hospital. One victim was treated for non-life threatening injuries. The other victim, an 88-year-old woman, later succumbed to her injuries.  The driver, Reginald Cousins Jr (DOB: 11/16/1966), was arrested and charged with Driving Under the Influence, Aggravated Assault, Reckless Endangerment, Vehicular Assault, Pedestrians' Right-of-Way in Crosswalks, Failure to Exercise Due Care, and Light Law Violation. Additional charges are pending.  This information is preliminary and subject to change as the investigation continues. Chattanooga Police ask anyone with information regarding this incident to call 423-698-2525. The charges and allegations referenced in this release are merely accusations of criminal conduct, not evidence. A defendant is presumed innocent unless and until proven guilty beyond a reasonable doubt and convicted through due process of law. #CPDnews

Must be able to maintain good interpersonal relationships with staff, co-workers, managers and citizens. Must accomplish the essential functions of the job, with or without reasonable accommodations, in a timely manner. May be assigned or reassigned to any division within the department. Performs other related duties as required. Typical equipment operated might include, but is not limited to: tractor-trailers, low boys, fuel trucks, bucket trucks, mechanical street sweepers, knuckle-boom trucks, articulated boom mowers, oil distributors, jet-flushing/vacuum trucks, CCTV equipped trucks and automated garbage trucks with an articulated arm. Must be able to use electronic devices to receive and track work. Position requires minimal, but daily public interaction and must be customer service centered, focused, and able to recognize or resolve customer needs according to departmental practices. PHYSICAL DEMANDS: Positions in this class typically require climbing, balancing, stooping, kneeling, crouching, crawling, reaching, standing, walking, pushing, pulling, lifting, fingering, grasping, feeling, talking, hearing, seeing and repetitive motions. WORK ENVIRONMENT: Medium Work: Exerting up-to 50 pounds of force occasionally, and/or up-to 20 pounds of force frequently, and/or up-to 10 pounds of force constantly to move objects. Great reminder!! ⬇️⬇️⬇️🔥 Turning on the heat for the first time? Don’t panic if you smell something burning. It’s often just dust burning off your furnace parts after months of sitting idle. The smell should fade after a few minutes. If the smell doesn’t go away or gets stronger, turn off the heat and call an HVAC professional. And if you see smoke or suspect fire or gas fumes, call 911 immediately. Stay warm and stay safe! ❄️
